가게.ex: 이 가게는 밤 열 시에 문을 닫아요.
가게.e: Probably from an old word meaning 'makeshift house' — a simple street stall.

수건.x: Please give me one more towel.

주차.ex: 이 건물 앞에서는 주차를 할 수 없어요.
주차.x: You can't park in front of this building.

설날.x: On Lunar New Year's Day, families gather and eat rice cake soup.
설날.e: 설 'new year' + 날 'day'; people eat 떡국 and bow to elders (세배).
설날.t: Pronounced [설랄] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

마다.forms: Same form after any noun: 날마다, 주말마다, 사람마다
마다.ex: 저는 주말마다 집 근처 공원에서 운동해요.
마다.x: I exercise in the park near my house every weekend.
마다.t: 사람마다 달라요 'It differs from person to person' is a very handy pattern.

때문.x: I couldn't go to school because of a cold.
때문.t: Use 때문에 for reasons, but not with requests or suggestions; use -(으)니까 there instead.

대회.ex: 동생이 노래 대회에 나가서 일 등을 했어요.
대회.x: My younger sibling entered a singing contest and won first place.
대회.t: Enter a contest with 대회에 나가다; 말하기 대회 is a speech contest.

건배.x: Shall we all raise our glasses and make a toast?
건배.e: Literally 'dry the cup' — drain your glass.
건배.t: Say 건배! when clinking glasses. With elders, hold your glass with two hands and turn your head slightly away when you drink.

새다.m: to leak; to escape (of light, gas, or a secret)
새다.x: It's raining, and water is leaking from the ceiling.
새다.e: Homonym warning: 새다 also means 'to dawn,' as in 밤이 새다.
새다.t: Don't confuse 새다 'to leak' with 세다 'to be strong, to count'; they sound almost the same.

연주.x: That pianist's performance was truly beautiful.
연주.t: Use 연주하다 for instruments in formal contexts; in everyday speech 피아노를 치다 or 기타를 치다 is more common.

관람.m: viewing, watching (a show, game or exhibit)
관람.ex: 이 영화는 열다섯 살 이상 관람이 가능합니다.
관람.x: This movie may be viewed by those 15 and older.
관람.t: Pronounced [괄람]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

금지하다.m: to prohibit, to ban, to forbid
금지하다.ex: 정부는 공원에서 담배 피우는 것을 금지했습니다.
금지하다.x: The government banned smoking in parks.

반면.m: the other side; whereas, on the other hand
반면.ex: 이 집은 넓은 반면 교통이 불편해요.
반면.x: This house is spacious, but on the other hand, transportation is inconvenient.
반면.t: Attach it to a modifier to contrast two facts: -(으)ㄴ/는 반면(에).

거래하다.m: to deal, to trade, to do business
거래하다.ex: 저희 회사는 그 회사와 10년 동안 거래했어요.
거래하다.x: Our company has done business with that company for ten years.
거래하다.e: Literally 'go and come': goods and money moving back and forth.

전통적.x: On Lunar New Year, people eat traditional food.
전통적.e: 전통 'tradition' + -적 '-al': turns nouns into describing words: 역사적, 문화적.
전통적.t: Use 전통적인 before nouns and 전통적으로 as an adverb.

발달하다.ex: 인터넷이 발달해서 정보를 쉽게 찾을 수 있어요.
발달하다.x: Because the internet has developed, we can find information easily.
발달하다.e: Literally 'to set out and reach' a higher level.
발달하다.t: 발달 is common for technology, the body or skills; 발전 is preferred for countries and economies.

포근하다.x: Even though it's winter, the weather is mild like spring today.
포근하다.e: Think of a soft blanket: used for bedding, hugs, and mild winter days.

화폐.x: Long ago, people used seashells as money.
화폐.e: Literally 'goods and silk' — things once used to pay before coins.
화폐.t: 화폐 is the formal or academic word; in daily life just say 돈.

방송사.ex: 그 방송사는 뉴스와 드라마를 모두 만들어요.
방송사.x: That broadcaster makes both news and dramas.

수면.x: Getting enough sleep is very important for your health.
수면.e: Both syllables mean 'sleep'. Homonym: 수면 'water surface'.
수면.t: 수면 is formal or medical; in everyday speech say 잠.

발레.ex: 연말에는 가족과 함께 발레 공연을 보러 가요.
발레.x: At the end of the year, I go to see a ballet performance with my family.
발레.e: From French 'ballet'; the final 't' is silent, as in English.

서예.x: My grandfather practices calligraphy every morning.
서예.e: Literally 'writing art' — the art of brush writing.

산림.ex: 지난봄에 난 산불로 넓은 산림이 사라졌어요.
산림.x: A large area of forest was lost in the wildfire last spring.
산림.t: Pronounced [살림], the same sound as 살림 (housekeeping); context tells them apart.

배기가스.ex: 자동차 배기가스는 대기 오염의 큰 원인이에요.
배기가스.x: Car exhaust is a major cause of air pollution.
배기가스.e: Literally 'expelled-air gas'; 가스 is from English 'gas'.

연민.ex: 그는 가난한 사람들에게 깊은 연민을 느꼈어요.
연민.x: He felt deep compassion for poor people.
연민.e: Two syllables that both mean 'pity', doubled for emphasis.

행복감.ex: 가족과 함께 있을 때 행복감을 느껴요.
행복감.x: I feel happy when I'm with my family.
행복감.e: Literally 'the feeling of good fortune and blessing'.

마찬가지.ex: 저도 마찬가지예요. 매운 음식을 잘 못 먹어요.
마찬가지.x: Same here. I can't really eat spicy food.
마찬가지.e: Probably from 마치 'just like' + 한가지 'the same kind'.

전략적.x: The company strategically expanded into overseas markets.
전략적.e: -적 turns a noun into '-ic/-al': 전략적, 정서적, 추상적.

탑승권.x: Sir/Ma'am, please show your boarding pass and passport.
탑승권.t: Pronounced [탑씅꿘] — tensing after ㅂ and in -권.

체조.x: Every morning I do some light exercises in the park.

씨름.x: On Chuseok I watched a ssireum tournament with my family.
씨름.e: Native word. The top champion of a big tournament is called 천하장사 'strongest under heaven'.
씨름.t: Wrestlers grip each other's cloth thigh band (샅바) and win by making the opponent touch the sand with any body part above the knee.

유포.ex: 허위 정보를 유포하면 처벌을 받을 수 있습니다.
유포.x: Spreading false information can be punished.

변모하다.m: to transform, to change in appearance
변모하다.ex: 작은 어촌이 세계적인 관광 도시로 변모했습니다.
변모하다.x: A small fishing village transformed into a world-class tourist city.

고안하다.m: to devise, to invent, to design
고안하다.ex: 그는 물을 절약하는 새로운 장치를 고안했어요.
고안하다.x: He devised a new device for saving water.

쏟아붓다.forms: 쏟아부어요 · 쏟아부었어요 · 쏟아부을 거예요 · 쏟아부으세요 (ㅅ irregular)
쏟아붓다.m: to pour in (money, effort); to pour out (all); to shower (with criticism)
쏟아붓다.ex: 그는 이 사업에 전 재산을 쏟아부었어요.
쏟아붓다.x: He poured his entire fortune into this business.
쏟아붓다.e: 쏟다 'to spill, to pour' + 붓다 'to pour' — pouring out every last drop.
쏟아붓다.t: Conjugates like 붓다: 쏟아부어요, never 쏟아붓어요.

안하무인.m: arrogance, acting as if no one else matters
안하무인.ex: 돈이 많다고 안하무인으로 행동하면 안 돼요.
안하무인.x: Just because you're rich doesn't mean you can act like no one else matters.
안하무인.e: Literally 'no one below one's eyes' — looking down on everyone.

허심탄회.x: Let's talk openly and honestly today.
허심탄회.e: Literally 'an empty mind and a level, open heart'.

원천.ex: 어릴 때부터 해 온 독서는 제 창의력의 원천이에요.
원천.x: Reading, which I've done since childhood, is the source of my creativity.
원천.e: Literally 'source spring' — where water first wells up.

팔자.x: He laughed, saying he was just destined to have a hard life.
팔자.e: Literally 'eight characters' — birth year, month, day and hour used in fortune-telling.
팔자.t: Pronounced [팔짜]; 팔자가 좋다 = to have an easy, lucky life.

소확행.m: small but certain happiness, little everyday pleasures
소확행.ex: 퇴근 후에 맥주 한 잔이 제 소확행이에요.
소확행.x: A glass of beer after work is my little everyday happiness.
소확행.e: Short for 소소하지만 확실한 행복 'small but certain happiness' (小確幸), a phrase from a Japanese writer's essay.
소확행.t: A trend word since about 2018. Pronounced [소화캥].

균형가격.ex: 수요와 공급이 만나는 점에서 균형가격이 결정됩니다.
균형가격.x: The equilibrium price is set where supply and demand meet.

절대주의.x: Seventeenth-century France is a classic example of an absolutist monarchy.
절대주의.t: 절대 alone is a strong adverb, 'never' or 'absolutely': 절대 안 돼요! (Absolutely not!)

유행병.ex: 옛날에는 유행병으로 많은 사람이 목숨을 잃었어요.
유행병.x: In the old days, many people lost their lives to epidemics.
유행병.e: Literally 'disease that is in fashion' — it spreads like a trend.

어조.ex: 그는 차분한 어조로 자신의 의견을 말했어요.
어조.x: He stated his opinion in a calm tone.
어조.e: Literally 'word tune' — the attitude a speaker's words carry.

다분하다.m: considerable, quite a lot (esp. of likelihood)
다분하다.x: There's a good chance that plan will fail.
다분하다.t: Typically 가능성이 다분하다 or 소지가 다분하다 — 'there's a good chance of (something bad)'.

유예하다.m: to postpone, to defer, to suspend (a decision, payment or sentence)
유예하다.ex: 정부는 세금 납부 기한을 석 달 유예하기로 했습니다.
유예하다.x: The government decided to defer the tax payment deadline by three months.
유예하다.e: Literally 'hesitate and delay' — putting something off for a set time.
유예하다.t: 집행유예 'suspended sentence' and 유예 기간 'grace period' are the most common collocations.

지음.m: a true friend who understands you completely, a soulmate friend
지음.ex: 그는 나를 진정으로 이해해 주는 지음이에요.
지음.x: He is a true friend who really understands me.
지음.e: Literally 'one who knows the sound' — a friend who alone understood a musician's playing.
지음.t: Literary and rare in speech; 지음 also means 'making' from 짓다, so context matters.
